review_notes: Reviewed all 119 lines, the underlying graph definitions, relevant measurability APIs, and downstream uses of label injectivity. Found one useful generalisation requiring no new mathematics. Proposed statements were not checked by executing Lean.

findings.excerpt:
theorem measurable_injective_labels :
    Measurable (fun U : ℕ → ℝ => Function.Injective U) := by
  exact Measurable.forall (fun u => Measurable.forall (fun v =>
    ((measurable_pi_apply u).eq (measurable_pi_apply v)).imp measurable_const))
findings.problem: The injectivity event is unnecessarily restricted to natural-number indices and real labels. The proof uses only countability of the index type and measurability of equality on the label space, not any arithmetic or order structure.
findings.proposed_change:
Generalise the statements to:

 theorem measurable_injective_labels {ι β : Type*} [Countable ι]
     [MeasurableSpace β] [MeasurableEq β] :
     Measurable (fun U : ι → β => Function.Injective U)

 theorem measurableSet_injective_labels {ι β : Type*} [Countable ι]
     [MeasurableSpace β] [MeasurableEq β] :
     MeasurableSet {U : ι → β | Function.Injective U}

The existing proofs have the required general form: coordinate evaluations are measurable, Measurable.eq uses MeasurableEq β, and the two Measurable.forall applications use Countable ι. The equality of indices remains a constant measurable predicate. Keep the set theorem as the .setOf corollary. No Nonempty or infinitude assumptions are needed: empty index types give a constantly true predicate, and empty label spaces or finite types cause no exceptional case.
findings.benefit: Makes the same collision-event API available for finite or other countable vertex types and for discrete, vector, or tuple-valued labels, without encoding labels into ℝ or reproving the argument. Existing ℕ → ℝ applications remain specialisations.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem measurable_pi_apply (a : δ) : Measurable fun f : ∀ a, X a => f a :=
  measurable_pi_iff.1 measurable_id a

theorem Measurable.eq {m : MeasurableSpace α} [MeasurableSpace β] [MeasurableEq β]
    {f g : α → β} (hf : Measurable f) (hg : Measurable g) : Measurable fun x => f x = g x :=

lemma Measurable.forall [Countable ι] {p : ι → α → Prop} (hp : ∀ i, Measurable (p i)) :
    Measurable fun a ↦ ∀ i, p i a :=

def Injective (f : α → β) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃a₁ a₂⦄, f a₁ = f a₂ → a₁ = a₂
